name: Mulholland Drive
blurb: David Lynch's Hollywood mystery about a hopeful actress and a woman with amnesia
title: Mulholland Drive Explained: Plot Summary and Ending
description: Mulholland Drive explained: who is who, the plot in order, the blue box, Club Silencio, Lynch's 10 clues and the ending explained.
h1: Mulholland Drive Explained: Plot, Characters and Ending
answer: Mulholland Drive (styled Mulholland Dr.) is a 2001 mystery film written and directed by David Lynch, starring Naomi Watts and Laura Harring. It began as a pilot for an ABC television series; when the network turned it down, Lynch shot new material with French funding and turned it into a feature. A dark-haired woman survives a car crash on Mulholland Drive above Los Angeles, loses her memory and hides in an apartment, where Betty, a cheerful young actress newly arrived in Hollywood, finds her. The two set out to discover who she is, while a film director is forced by sinister figures to cast an unknown actress in his movie.

head: Character
Who they are
rows: An aspiring actress from Deep River, Ontario, staying in her aunt Ruth's Hollywood apartment
A woman with amnesia after a crash, who takes her name from a Rita Hayworth poster
A film director being pressured over who to cast as his lead
The blonde unknown actress Adam is told to cast
The Castigliane brothers and Mr. Roque
Mob-like backers who control the film from behind the scenes
A quiet, menacing man who gives Adam instructions
The manager of Betty's apartment building
A man who describes a nightmare about the Winkie's diner on Sunset Boulevard

body: Beginning. The film opens with dancers at a jitterbug contest, a beaming young woman, and a shot of a bed. Then, on Mulholland Drive at night, a limousine stops and its driver points a gun at the dark-haired passenger, but a carload of joyriders smashes into it. She staggers down into Hollywood and sneaks into an apartment whose owner, Ruth, is leaving town. Betty Elms arrives from Canada to stay in her aunt Ruth's flat, finds the stranger in the shower, and the woman calls herself Rita after a poster. In her purse are a large amount of cash and an odd blue key. Separately, at a diner called Winkie's, a man named Dan tells a friend he dreamed of a horrifying figure behind the building; they go out back, the figure appears and Dan collapses. Director Adam Kesher is told by the Castigliane brothers that a woman named Camilla Rhodes must get the lead in his film. He refuses, finds his wife in bed with another man, has his money cut off, and is told by the Cowboy to cast her. A hitman, Joe, kills a man for a book of phone numbers and botches it.

Middle. Rita remembers one name, Diane Selwyn. Betty gives an astonishing audition for a casting agent, then visits Adam's set, where their eyes meet just as Adam announces the role will go to Camilla Rhodes. Betty and Rita find Diane Selwyn's apartment and break in; on the bed is a woman's decomposing body. Rita, shaken, puts on a blonde wig so she looks like Betty, and that night the two women become lovers.

At 2 a.m. Rita wakes repeating the word silencio and takes Betty to Club Silencio, a theatre where a host insists that everything is a recording and there is no band. A singer performs a Spanish version of Roy Orbison's Crying, collapses, and the song goes on without her. Both women weep. Betty finds a blue box in her bag. Back at the apartment, she vanishes; Rita unlocks the box with her key, it is empty and dark, and she disappears too.

End. The Cowboy says it is time to wake up. A woman who looks like Betty, now gaunt and bitter, wakes in Diane Selwyn's apartment: this is Diane. In her life, she is a struggling actress who came to Hollywood after winning a jitterbug contest, and she was the lover of Camilla Rhodes, played by the actress who played Rita. Camilla, a star, helped her get small parts, then broke it off and became involved with Adam. At a dinner party at Adam's house on Mulholland Drive, Diane watches Camilla kiss a blonde woman, the one Diane's mind earlier called Camilla, and hears that Camilla and Adam will marry. At Winkie's, Diane gives Joe cash and a photo of Camilla. He tells her that when the job is done she will find a blue key.

What the film shows: the blue key sits on Diane's coffee table, meaning Camilla is dead. Behind Winkie's, the figure from Dan's dream holds the blue box, and a tiny elderly couple, who earlier said goodbye to Betty at the airport, crawl out of it. Diane, wracked by guilt, hallucinates; the couple, life-size and laughing, chase her into her bedroom, and she shoots herself. Smoke fills the room, the faces of Betty and Rita appear smiling over the city, and at Club Silencio a woman whispers the word silencio.

Lynch never explained the film. For the DVD release he included a card of 10 clues, among them: pay attention to the beginning, where at least two clues come before the credits; notice the red lampshade; notice where the accident happens; ask who gives a key and why; notice the robe, the ashtray and the coffee cup; ask what is felt and realised at Club Silencio; ask whether talent alone helped Camilla; and ask where Aunt Ruth is. The main readings, which remain debated:

ol: Dream, then reality. The most widely accepted reading. The first two hours are Diane's dream, or fantasy, after she has had Camilla killed. She recasts herself as the talented, innocent Betty, turns Camilla into Rita, a helpless woman who needs her, makes Adam a humiliated man and blames shadowy forces for Camilla's success. The real details leak in: the key, the body, the name Diane Selwyn, the diner. The last half hour shows her real life and suicide. Lynch's clues fit this reading, from the bed before the credits to Aunt Ruth, who in reality has died and left Diane money.
Dying vision. Some critics read the closing images, and possibly much of the film, as Diane's last moments of consciousness, with Club Silencio as the point where the illusion is exposed.

No single key. Others argue that dream and reality are mixed throughout and the film is meant to be felt rather than solved; critic J. Hoberman called it a poisonous valentine to Hollywood. Still other theories treat Betty and Diane as two different people, or the story as a loop or parallel worlds.

ul: Hollywood dreams: the film contrasts the fantasy of arriving in Los Angeles and becoming a star with the humiliation and envy of real failure.
Identity and doubling: actors play two characters each, and names, faces and roles slide from one person to another.
Desire and jealousy: Diane's love for Camilla turns into the possessiveness that leads to murder.
Illusion: Club Silencio's message that everything is a recording is a statement about film itself, which makes viewers feel real emotion over something that is not there.
Guilt: the blue key, the box and the elderly couple are guilt returning in forms Diane cannot escape.
Runtime: 146 minutes. English-language, with one song sung in Spanish; premiered at Cannes in May 2001, where Lynch shared the best director prize.
Origin: about 90 minutes of the film were shot as a TV pilot in 1999; the ending was written and shot later for the feature, which explains its abrupt change of tone.
Content: rated R in the US; includes explicit sex scenes, violence, a suicide and strong language.
How to watch: the film is built to be rewatched; Lynch's 10 clues are most useful on a second viewing.

check.q: What does Rita find in her purse?
options: A lot of cash and a blue key
A script and a bus ticket
check.why: The cash and the blue key are her only clues to who she is.

check.q: In the last part of the film, who is Diane Selwyn?
options: A struggling actress who was Camilla's lover
check.why: Diane, played by Naomi Watts, is the bitter actress whose affair with Camilla has ended.

check.q: What does the blue key on Diane's table mean?
options: She has been cast in Adam's film
check.why: Joe told Diane that a blue key would be left for her when the job was done.

faq.q: Who is the man behind Winkie's in Mulholland Drive?
faq.a: The film never says. In the dream reading he stands for the fear and guilt behind Diane's crime, which she arranged at that diner; at the end he holds the blue box.

faq.q: What did David Lynch say Mulholland Drive means?
faq.a: He refused to explain it. The only guidance he gave was a list of 10 clues printed with the DVD release, pointing viewers to details like the red lampshade, the key and Aunt Ruth.

faq.q: Is the dead body in Diane Selwyn's apartment Diane?
faq.a: In the most common reading the body is Diane after her suicide, which the dream glimpses ahead of time, but the film does not confirm it and some critics have other views.
